gaps.sentence: Scarcely had she opened the letter ___ she burst into tears.
gaps.explanation: 'Scarcely... when' marks the immediate consequence of the first event.

gaps.sentence: You can stay up late tonight ___ it's a school night tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless it's a school night' = if it isn't a school night.

gaps.sentence: He was warned repeatedly; ___, he ignored every safety rule.
gaps.explanation: He ignored the warnings despite receiving them: nevertheless marks that contrast.

gaps.sentence: He spends money ___ it grew on trees.
gaps.explanation: 'As if it grew on trees' — the unreal comparison justifies the criticism.

gaps.sentence: The old system charged per download, ___ the new one uses a flat monthly fee.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' sets the old and new systems side by side.

gaps.sentence: The plan was expensive; ___, the board approved it.
gaps.explanation: The approval happens in spite of the cost: nevertheless signals concession.

gaps.sentence: ___ he had studied hard, he failed the exam.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a full clause; due/owing take noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: ___ his impressive qualifications, he wasn't even shortlisted.
